chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Suleym the freedman of Tarbaal, who said: Hisham narrated to me from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The people are upon six categories.'
He said: I said, 'Do you permit me to write it down?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'What shall I write?' He said, 'Write: The people of threat are from the people of Paradise and the people of Hell.'
And write: And others have confessed their sins, they have mingled a good deed and an evil one.
He said: I said, 'Who are these?' He said, 'Wahshi is among them.'
And write: And others are those of whom delay is made, awaiting Allah's command; whether He will punish them or turn to them (mercifully).
He said: And write: Except the weak from among the men and the women and the children, who have not the power to find a way.
They cannot find a way to disbelief, nor can they find a way to faith; so these, it may be, Allah will pardon them.
He said: And write: The people of Al-Araf.

I said, 'And what are the people of Al-Araf?' He said: 'A people whose good deeds and evil deeds are equal. So if He enters them into the Fire, it is due to their sins, and if He enters them into Paradise, it is due to His Mercy.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْأَعْرَافِ: The people of Al-Araf (a barrier or elevated place between Paradise and Hell)
key_terms.أَهْلُ الْوَعِيدِ: People of threat (those promised punishment but may be forgiven)
key_terms.الْوَحْشِيُّ: Wahshi (the killer of Hamza, cited as an example of mixed deeds)

ai.seo_question: What are the six categories of people and their fates according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) categorizes humanity into six groups, offering a nuanced Shia eschatology that balances divine justice with mercy. This classification highlights the unique status of the 'People of Al-Araf' (Ahl al-A'raf), whose equal good and bad deeds place them in a liminal state awaiting God's final decree, and the 'Murj'ah', whose fate is suspended between punishment and forgiveness. The inclusion of Wahshi, the killer of Hamza, among those who mixed deeds illustrates the profound capacity for repentance even for major sinners, while the 'Mustad'afin' (weak) are excused due to their inability to comprehend or choose the path of faith.
